chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Billie Holiday crying at Ciro's
summary: Billie Holiday came to Ciro's in Los Angeles around 1959 to pour out her regret about heroin, shortly before she died.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Now, I remember I was working at Ciro's out in Los Angeles, with Nat Cole, and we were getting ready to do the last show and the waiter came back to me and said, Mr. Collins, will you please come outside, there's a lady out here who's cursing and giving me hell, and told me if I didn't get you she's going to kick my ass, you know. Okay. I'll come right out. And I went right out, it was Billie Holiday. So I sat at the table with her and she had to see me because she had to talk to someone, and she sat there and she cried and told me how sorry she was that she could not beat this shit, that it had -- that she tried, she don't want any sex life, she's sick all the time, she's been hounded, and she sat here. And I just told her, well go ahead and let it all out. And she just cried, and I -- because we knew each other so well, that you know -- and how she regretted having let this thing get -- just kill her. And then shortly after that she died.

This was around 195 -- I don't know, '9 or sometimes when Ciro's was open. Towards the last, when it was open. Because before that she had appeared in Vegas, she had started singing those clubs in Vegas, you know. But not -- just a shell of her former self. But she came in this club this night and she wanted to just pour her heart out.

And I cried with her, you know, because I just knew her so well and I loved her so well, you know. But this is what -- so it's no way that I could get hooked on anything and see what it has done to these great people. You know, great performers, great entertainers, great musicians. You know. So it can't be any good.

No, it can't be any good. And I don't think that it didn't help. Maybe -- I'm sure that -- now with Billie I don't say that it was a social reasons or anything that she started. I think Billie did because this guy did, you know. She was influenced by Jimmie Monroe. So I believe this is why she did, but we come back to the musicians.
